''For neither Peter'' ({{ls}}aith S. And S. Augu{{ls}}tine ep. 19. c. 2 in fine. ''That'' ({{ls}}aith he) ''which vvas done of Paul profitably by the libertie of charitie, the {{ls}}ame Peter tooke in good part by holy and benigne godlines of humilitie, and {{ls}}o he gaue vnto po{{ls}}teritie a more rare and holy example, if at any time perhaps they did amis, to be content to be corrected of their iuniors, then Paul, for to be bold and confident: yea the inferiors to re{{ls}}i{{ls}}t their betters for defending the truth of the Go{{ls}}pel, brotherly charitie alvvaies pre{{ls}}erued''. {{outside R|It proueth nothing agai{{ls}}t Peters {{ls}}uperioritie, that he vvas reprehended.}}By which notable {{ls}}peaches of the Doctors vve may al{{ls}}o {{ls}}ee, how friuolou{{ls}}ly the Heretikes argue herevpon, that S. Peter could not be Superior to S. Paul, being {{ls}}o reprehended of him: vvhereas the Fathers make it an example to the Superiors, to beare vvith humilitie the correption or controulement euen of their inferiors.
